description_full: JBS N.V., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the processing of animal proteins, encompassing activities related to beef, pork, lamb, and poultry worldwide. The company is involved in the production and marketing of prepared foods and other related products, as well as operations in leather, collagen, hygiene and beauty products, metal packaging, biodiesel, and other related businesses. It offers its products under the Seara, Doriana, Pilgrim's, Moy Park, Primo, Friboi, Maturatta, Swift, Ozo, Adaptable Meals, and other brand names. The company was founded in 1953 and is based in Amstelveen, the Netherlands.

financial_summary: JBS N.V. is a large-cap consumer defensive business with a $13.4B market cap on $86.2B of annual revenue.

Returns on capital run at 14% against a 9% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 13% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $833M in free cash flow — roughly 1 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.31× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.6× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 11.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 58% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
